summary: Backend-only testing of PUT /api/admin/rental-contracts/{contract_id} (late_fee_amount sync to pending invoices). 10/10 pytest cases PASSED. Verified: (1) late_fee_amount persisted; (2) legacy alias `late_fee` correctly mapped to late_fee_amount; (3) on late_fee change, pending rental_payments with late_fee>0 are recalculated (late_fee + total_due updated, late_fee_synced_from_contract=true) and response.synced_pending_invoices reflects count; (4) pending invoices with late_fee==0 are NOT touched; (5) when late_fee_amount is unchanged, no sync runs; (6) other editable fields (rent_amount, payment_due_day, late_fee_grace_days) still persist; (7) 404 returned for unknown contract_id. Note: the supervisor-managed backend at port 8001 is the ross-tax-api (/app/backend), NOT ross-house-backend — I started /app/ross-house-backend on port 8011 (uvicorn) to run the tests against the actual contracts_router.py code.

minor.issue: When late_fee sync writes to an invoice, total_paid logic uses old total_due to decide if 'fully paid' (line 703). For a pending invoice this is irrelevant (status='pending'), but if the same code path is ever reused for partially-paid invoices it may set total_paid=new_total even though tenant hasn't actually paid the new fee — review if business logic ever extends this sync to partially-paid invoices.

old_late_fee read from contract.get('late_fee_amount') but legacy contracts may store the value under 'late_fee'. Two existing docs in DB could have late_fee stored only as 'late_fee'; consider falling back: float(contract.get('late_fee_amount') or contract.get('late_fee') or 0).

action_items: (optional) Add fallback `contract.get('late_fee_amount') or contract.get('late_fee') or 0` when computing old_late_fee, to correctly detect changes on legacy contracts that only have the `late_fee` field.

(optional) Reconsider the total_paid recalculation in the sync block (line 703) — it currently assumes fully-paid if total_paid >= old total_due; for status='pending' invoices this is fine, but if filter ever broadens this could overstate payments.
critical_code_review_comments: PUT endpoint correctly performs sync only when |new - old| > 0.001 (good guard against float jitter).
Sync filter `status='pending' AND late_fee > 0` correctly excludes not-yet-late invoices — matches expected behavior.
Response now exposes `synced_pending_invoices` count and an updated success message — good for admin UX.
Error handling: sync block wrapped in try/except so a sync failure does NOT roll back the contract update (logs and continues).
File size: contracts_router.py is 2532 lines — should be split into smaller modules (e.g., addendums, checklist, signatures, recurring) in a follow-up refactor.
seed_data_creation: Tests insert one TEST contract per test (with _test_marker='test_rental_contract_late_fee_sync') plus 1-2 pending rental_payments. All are deleted in pytest fixture teardown. Verified 0 residual docs in Mongo after the run.

rca_of_issue: Original bug: changing contract.late_fee_amount didn't update existing pending invoices. Fix in /app/ross-house-backend/rental/contracts_router.py lines 685-717 — after the contract update, iterate rental_payments where status='pending' AND late_fee>0 and write {late_fee: new, total_due: amount+new, late_fee_synced_from_contract: true}. Response includes synced_pending_invoices count. Verified end-to-end via 10 pytest cases that the fix works as designed: latest-applied late fees on pending invoices now match the contract; invoices not yet flagged late (late_fee=0) are intentionally left for the cron to handle.
